metaDescription: Plan scuba diving and freediving in Kaş, Türkiye: top wrecks and reefs, clearest visibility months, water temps, and PADI/TSSF checks.
quickAnswer: Kaş is Türkiye's premier scuba diving and freediving hub, offering 30+ offshore sites within a 15–25 minute boat ride, steep limestone walls, intentional aircraft wrecks, and 25–30m visibility. Peak warm-water conditions run June through October (24–28°C), and every reputable operator holds both international PADI/CMAS/SSI accreditation and a current Turkish Underwater Sports Federation (TSSF) license.

body.text: Why is Kaş rated Türkiye's top diving destination?

Kaş sits along a deep Mediterranean shelf where rocky headlands and offshore islets drop rapidly from 5m to beyond 40m with minimal river silt, creating exceptional year-round clarity. According to [PADI's Kaş diving overview](https://www.padi.com/diving-in/kas/), divers can reach more than 30 distinct reef, cavern, canyon, and wreck sites directly from the town harbour.

That same steep bathymetry and sheltered bay network make Kaş an internationally respected freediving training ground, hosting line-training buoys in calm morning water. Underwater, expect loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta), dusky groupers, moray eels, barracuda schools, and scattered ancient Lycian amphorae—all protected under strict no-touch archaeological rules.
Which dive sites (Canyon, Dakota Plane Wreck, Flying Fish) suit beginners vs advanced divers?

Open Water beginners thrive on shallow bays and the upper rim of Canyon (5–18m), where gentle contours and light currents build buoyancy confidence. Advanced Open Water and deep-certified divers head for the C-47 Dakota Plane Wreck (18–26m), the Dimitri Wreck at the base of Canyon, and the offshore Flying Fish reef (20–60m+), which features strong currents and deep walls.

body.text: What months have the clearest 25–30m visibility and warmest water?

Visibility routinely reaches 25–30m from late May through November, with peak clarity often arriving in September and October once summer plankton blooms subside and boat traffic thins. Sea temperatures climb from 21°C in May to 27–28°C in August and September, holding a comfortable 23–24°C well into late October.

In July and August, a 3mm shorty or full suit suffices for recreational depths, though a 5mm wetsuit is smart if you plan repeated dives below the 20m thermocline or longer freediving sessions. Winter diving (December–April) remains possible with 16–18°C water and 7mm wetsuits, though fewer boats run daily schedules.
How do you verify PADI/CMAS licensed dive centres?

In Türkiye, legal commercial diving requires dual compliance: an active permit from the [Turkish Underwater Sports Federation (TSSF)](https://www.tssf.gov.tr/) displayed at the shop alongside verifiable international affiliation. Cross-check PADI centres directly on the [PADI Kaş Dive Shops directory](https://www.padi.com/dive-shops/kas/), where long-running local operators such as [Nautilus Dive Center](https://www.padi.com/dive-center/turkey/nautilus-dive-center/) and [Subaqua Diving Centre](https://www.padi.com/dive-center/turkey/subaqua-diving-centre/) list active ratings and courses.

items: Confirm the centre's valid TSSF authorisation certificate and emergency oxygen kit on board the boat.
Check instructor-to-student ratios (no more than 4–6 certified divers per guide on deep or current-prone sites).
Ask whether air fills come from an inspected, regularly tested compressor and whether Nitrox (EAN32) is available.
Verify boat boarding times (typically two single-tank boat trips daily, morning and afternoon) and surface-interval policies.
Bring your physical or digital certification card, logbook, and a medical fitness clearance if answering "yes" on the RSTC medical form.

faq.q: Can non-certified travellers try scuba diving in Kaş?
faq.a: Yes. Licensed centres run half-day Discover Scuba Diving (DSD) experiences in sheltered bays with 1-to-1 instructor supervision down to a maximum of 5–12 metres, requiring no prior certification.

faq.q: How many dives can I do in one day in Kaş?
faq.a: Most Kaş dive boats return to harbour between dives rather than staying out all day, running a morning dive (around 09:30) and an afternoon dive (around 14:30), plus occasional scheduled night dives.

faq.q: Is it legal to touch or collect ancient amphorae underwater?
faq.a: No. Turkish cultural-heritage law strictly prohibits touching, moving, or removing any archaeological artifacts from the seabed, with severe legal penalties. Buoyancy control is essential around amphora fields.

faq.q: Which airport is closest to Kaş for dive travellers?
faq.a: Dalaman Airport (DLM) is roughly 2 hours 15 minutes west by private transfer, while Antalya Airport (AYT) is about 3 hours east. Remember to leave at least 18–24 hours after your final dive before flying or driving over high mountain passes.

faq.q: Are there freediving schools in Kaş?
faq.a: Yes. Several dedicated AIDA and SSI freediving schools operate out of Kaş from May to October, offering depth courses, equalization workshops, and guided fun dives over shallow reefs and wrecks.

faq.q: Do I need my own dive computer in Kaş?
faq.a: While dive guides carry computers and many shops rent them for a small daily fee, bringing your own dive computer is strongly recommended if you plan multi-day repetitive diving or Nitrox dives.
